body.p: This is a full and timely response to the Office action dated October 24, 2024.
Reexamination and reconsideration in view of the foregoing amendments and following remarks is respectfully solicited.

Claims 1-19 are pending in this application, with claims 1, 8, and 13 being the independent claims. Claims 1-3, 9, 13, and 14 have been amended herein. The specification has also been amended herein to correct a minor informality. No new matter is believed to have been added.

Claims 9 and 13 were objected to for various minor informalities. In response, these claims have been amended herein to cure the noted informalities. As such, reconsideration and withdrawal of the claim objections is requested.

Claims 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16, and 18 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 102 as allegedly being anticipated by a non-patent literature document entitled, "Fault Tolerant Electromechanical Actuators for Aircraft," and authored by John William Bennett (Bennett). This rejection is respectfully traversed.
Independent claims 1, 8, and 13 each recite, inter alia, a plurality of actuator
It is alleged in the Office action that the triplex motor control unit (MCU)
limitations (i) and (ii) of the independent claims. For at least the following reasons, it is submitted that this allegation is wholly erroneous.

Firstly, as Figure 4-24 (and the associated text) of Bennett discloses, each MCU processing lane receives actuator positions signals from each of the actuator position sensors, and not from a different one of the actuator position sensors.

Secondly, the Office action points to the median functional blocks in Figure 4-24 and the mean functional blocks in Figure 4-28 as somehow functioning to combine the motor position data and the actuator position data into a single sensor data packet. However, these functional blocks implement voting schemes, which select which of the multiple actuator position signals to process. These functional blocks explicitly do not process and combine the motor position data and the actuator position data into a single sensor data packet.

Bennett discloses a generic, well-known architecture of multiple conventional (RVDT/Resolver) sensors that are cross-communicated to the controllers, cross- communicated, and voted upon for fault tolerance. The instant claims are directed to a "local-to-the-actuator" sensor architecture that uses processors to combine motor and actuator sensor data into a single communication packet. These features are clearly not disclosed, or even remotely suggested, in Bennett.

"A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631, 2 USPQ2d 1051, 1053 (Fed. Cir. 1987). "When a claim covers several structures or compositions, either generically or as alternatives, the claim is deemed anticipated if any of the structures or compositions within the scope of the claim is known in the prior art." Brown v. 3M, 265 F.3d 1349, 1351, 60 USPQ2d 1375, 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2001) (claim to a system for setting a computer clock to an offset time to address the Year 2000 (Y2K) problem, applicable to records with year date data in "at least one of two-digit, three-digit, or four-digit" representations, was held anticipated by a system that offsets year dates in only two-digit formats. "The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the ... claim." Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236, 9 USPQ2d 1913, 1920 (Fed. Cir. 1989). The elements must be arranged as required by the claim, but this is not an

ipsissimis verbis test, i.e., identity of terminology is not required. In re Bond, 910 F.2d 831, 15 USPQ2d 1566 (Fed. Cir. 1990). Because Bennett fails to meet this legal standard, it does not and cannot anticipate the claims.
In view of the foregoing, reconsideration and withdrawal of the § 102 rejections is respectfully requested.

Claims 3, 5, 10, 15, and 17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Bennett and Official Notice; and claims 7, 12, and 19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Bennett, Official Notice, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2023/0152822 (Wiegman). These rejections are respectfully traversed.
While not conceding to the Examiner's alleged Official Notice, nor conceding
that Wiegman discloses or suggests all that is alleged in the Office action, it is submitted that neither alleged finding make up for the deficiencies of Bennett that are delineated above.
In view of the foregoing, reconsideration and withdrawal of the § 103 rejections is respectfully requested.

Based on the above, independent Claims 1, 8, and 15 are patentable over the citations of record. The dependent claims are also deemed patentable for the reasons given above with respect to the independent claims and because each recite features which are patentable in its own right. Individual consideration of the dependent claims is respectfully solicited.
The other art of record is also not understood to disclose or suggest the inventive concept of the present invention as defined by the claims.
Hence, Applicant submits that the present application is in condition for
allowance. Favorable reconsideration and withdrawal of the objections and rejections set forth in the above-noted Office Action, and an early Notice of Allowance are requested.
